name: files
description: File-style storage: root-jailed host/temp filesystems and per-user DLFS drives (decentralised, signed, WebDAV-mountable). Load for reading or writing file content rather than structured lattice values.

content.inline:
## Files
Two mechanisms; pick by need:

**file** — venue-configured roots (host directories or temp scratch), root-jailed:
- roots lists what this venue offers; list/tree `{root, path}` browse; read `{root, path}` / write `{root, path, content}` move UTF-8 text; mkdir creates directories. Also under `v/ops/file/`: append, delete, stat.

**dlfs** — YOUR decentralised drives: per-user, signed, replicated lattice filesystems (also mountable over WebDAV when the venue enables it):
- list-drives shows yours; create-drive `{name}` makes one; read/write `{drive, path, content}` move file content; also under `v/ops/dlfs/`: list, tree, mkdir, append, delete, stat, delete-drive.

Choosing storage:
- Structured queryable state -> workspace (`w/`). Immutable shared values -> assets. File-shaped content, external tools, WebDAV access -> dlfs. Host-machine file exchange -> file roots.
- An asset can bind its content to a DLFS file (`content: {dlfs: path}`) — live document, stable identity.
- File ops act on the caller's authority: `file://` roots need explicit capability grants; dlfs drives are yours by ownership.
